seo_title: inDrive Case Study: Philippine Google Display Ads | SOMIN
description: SOMIN read 24 months of Philippine ride-hailing Google Ads, found no brand runs bespoke display creative, and built 108 inDrive banners on 3 pillars.
h1: inDrive's rivals buy app installs on Google, leaving brand display empty
lede: For inDrive, SOMIN analysed 24 months of Google Search, Display Network and YouTube ads from 7 ride-hailing and delivery brands in the Philippines, filtered to commuters. inDrive had 169 brand detections, behind Maxim and Angkas, and the category ran almost only automated app-install campaigns. SOMIN mapped the whitespace into 3 pillars and generated 108 display banners.
meta_line: A SOMIN brand briefing · Aug 2024 to Aug 2026 · Philippines · Commuters

challenge.title: Why the brief moved from Grab to inDrive and commuters
challenge.body: The brief started with Grab, but Grab had zero posts of its own on Google Ads in this workspace over 24 months; its measured paid media was 100% Facebook. The client redirected the brief to inDrive, which has a real Google Ads footprint, and shifted the audience focus to commuters. The question was where inDrive should play in Google paid media.

approach.title: 8 quarterly studies of commuter-filtered Google paid media
points: Used only Google Search, Search Partners, Display Network and YouTube ads, filtered to commuters, with no organic data.
Ran 8 quarterly studies to track tensions, personas and formats over 24 months.
Mapped inDrive's brand traits and product mix, then sorted narratives into owned, whitespace, contested and fading lanes.
Built 3 insight chains, each running from persona to tension, angle, story and proposition.
Drew brand colours and tone from inDrive's own organic posts for the art direction.

findings_title: App-install sameness, ownable fairness and Angkas-held safety

findings.title: One format for everyone
findings.body: In sampled category creatives, 194 of 194 in Year 1 and 179 of 185 in Year 2 were app campaigns with install calls to action. Nobody runs bespoke, brand-led display.

findings.title: Fairness is ownable
findings.body: Fairness is inDrive's most-tagged brand trait, with 91 detections ahead of Affordability at 75. Competitors talk generically about lower cost; none contest the agree-on-the-fare framing.

findings.title: Safety belongs to Angkas, for now
findings.body: A safety and trust theme recurs in at least 4 of 8 quarters, owned by Angkas at 85-100% share each time. inDrive's share of these themes is 0-3 posts in every quarter.

delivered.title: A whitespace map, 3 insight chains and 108 inDrive banners
points: A share-of-voice view of 7 brands on Google Ads over 24 months
A trend read across 8 quarters, with each shift labelled stable, falling or directional
A whitespace map: Fair Fare Control, Safety & Trust, Time & Traffic and a fading eco-conscious lane
3 insight chains, each from persona to tension, angle, story and propositions
108 display banners, 36 concepts per pillar across awareness, consideration and conversion, every headline and CTA at 9 words or fewer

quote.text: This is itself a whitespace: nobody in-category is running bespoke, brand-led Display creative

outcome.title: inDrive should own fare-setting and claim Safety & Trust
outcome.body: The brief recommends leaning inDrive's display creative into the “you set the fare together” claim, which is its alone in this channel, and claiming the Safety & Trust whitespace Angkas holds. On time and traffic, it suggests loss-aversion framing, a distinct angle rather than a louder version of the same congestion complaint.

faq.q: Why does the inDrive case mention Grab?
faq.a: Grab was the original subject, but it had no Google Ads posts of its own in the workspace over 24 months. The client redirected the brief to inDrive and to a commuter audience.

faq.q: What does the creative library include?
faq.a: 108 display banners generated with SOMIN image-generate and rendered in inDrive's brand identity: 36 per pillar, split into 12 awareness, 12 consideration and 12 conversion concepts.
Yes. Every figure traces to a workspace, profile, study, persona, tension, angle, story or proposition ID in the SOMIN platform, listed in the brief's audit trail.
